title: International sales and the CISG
summary: The CISG is the United Nations treaty on contracts for qualifying international sales of goods. Its own provisions can govern a sale instead of the domestic sales rules a reader might otherwise assume apply.
notes:
The assigned TeeVee Toons dispute concerned a buyer and a German machinery supplier. The court used the Convention’s treatment of intent and interpretation, including negotiations and conduct, to examine whether disputed printed terms and a merger clause were actually accepted. This matters because the parol evidence rule cannot simply be imported into a Convention case as though domestic law automatically controlled.

CISG Article 11 generally removes a writing requirement for the sales contract within its operation; that does not remove the need to establish agreement. Article 8 provides the interpretive framework discussed in the assigned supplemental opinion. These are distinct questions: how an agreement may be proved, what the parties meant, and whether they adopted a particular term.

Use the applicable treaty text to determine coverage and qualifications in a real problem. The casebook and supplied opinion support this comparison, but the complete assigned Selections text, with all relevant treaty provisions and declarations, is not present.
